svg.text: Peptide bond formation is a condensation (dehydration) reaction
Shaded on the left: the –OH of glycine's carboxyl and one H of alanine's amino group,
which leave together as water. The new C–N amide (peptide) bond has partial
double-bond character from resonance, so it is planar and does not rotate freely.
Hydrolysis (adding the water back) is thermodynamically favorable but very slow.
